pages.title: Shoots
pages.content: Packshot, lifestyle, detail and flat lay, and apparel and motion: four ways to fill a day in Bay A or Bay B. Each kind of shoot has its own page section, with what to send us and what you receive.

pages.title: Work

pages.title: Day rates
pages.content: Packshot day €1,450 / day, packshot half day €820 / half day, lifestyle set day €2,200 / day, apparel day €1,600 / day, video loop add-on €480 / shoot and €14 / extra retouched image. Prices exclude VAT.

pages.title: Book a shoot
pages.content: Send your product list to hello@kirinuki-studio.example. Theo replies within one working day and we hold a date for 5 working days while you confirm.

pages.title: About
pages.content: Ines Calloway founded Kirinuki Studio in 2014. Two bays, seven people, and one way of working: one sweep, one light, every first frame approved on the screen.

pages.title: Questions
pages.content: How much notice does a shoot day need? Two weeks. How long until I get my files? An online gallery within 3 working days and final files within 5 working days.

pages.title: Open dates list

pages.content: Kirinuki Studio, Unit 4, Wharf Yard, 22 Lantern Street, Harwick. Studio Mon–Fri 08:30–18:00. Email hello@kirinuki-studio.example or call +00 20 7946 0412.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content: We keep the product lists and email addresses you send us only to plan and deliver your shoot or to send the open dates list, and we do not share them.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content: A date is held for 5 working days. Cancellation is free until 10 working days before the shoot, 50% after. Finals come with unlimited commercial use for the client's own products. Invoices are due within 14 days.

posts.title: 48 bottles, one sweep
posts.excerpt: Ines Calloway on a packshot day for Alder & Moss: 48 frosted bottles, one sweep and a yes on the screen.
posts.content:
Alder & Moss came to us with 48 small frosted skincare bottles and one deadline: a whole range on their online shop in a week. We gave them a single packshot day in Bay A.

The morning went to the first bottle. Dev set the softbox over the sweep, Marta tethered the camera to the studio screen, and the client's two product managers stood behind her until the first frame matched their reference. Once they said yes, nothing about the light moved again.

From there it was a rhythm: place, check, shoot, swap the tray. Two angles each, front and a three-quarter turn, all 48 before late afternoon. Noor matched the colour across the set so the white of the cap read the same on bottle 1 and bottle 48.

The online gallery was with Alder & Moss on the third working day and the retouched finals on the fifth, cropped to the sizes their marketplace asks for. That is the whole story: one sweep, one light, one day, and a yes on the screen before we began.
